hotel.name: The Mitsui Kyoto, a Luxury Collection Hotel & Spa

verified_facts.text: The hotel is in the heart of Kyoto, adjacent to Nijo Castle, a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
verified_facts.excerpt: Located in the heart of Kyoto, adjacent to the legendary Nijo Castle, a UNESCO World Heritage Site

verified_facts.text: The hotel is built on a 250-year-old historic site that was once the home of the executive branch of the Mitsui family.
verified_facts.excerpt: The central Kyoto hotel is built on a 250-year-old historic site that was once the home of the executive branch of the Mitsui Family

verified_facts.text: Guests arrive through an ornate wooden gateway that once marked the entrance to the Mitsui clan's Kyoto residence.
verified_facts.excerpt: The ornate wooden gateway that guests pass through upon arrival offers a hint of its history: it once marked the entrance to the Kyoto residence of the Mitsui clan

verified_facts.text: Guest rooms are a modern reimagining of the traditional Japanese tearoom, with carefully chosen natural materials elevated using artisanal skills.
verified_facts.excerpt: A modern reimagining of the traditional Japanese tearoom, the 160 guest rooms feature carefully chosen natural materials, elevated using artisanal skills.

verified_facts.text: Interiors are by designer Andre Fu.
verified_facts.excerpt: Interior designer André Fu infused a philosophy of modernity, comfort and convenient luxury

verified_facts.text: Japanese architect Akira Kuryu was part of the hotel's creative team alongside Andre Fu.
verified_facts.excerpt: to Japanese architect Akira Kuryu

verified_facts.text: Bathtubs are fashioned out of stone and are generously sized.
verified_facts.excerpt: The bathtubs are fashioned out of stone, and their generous size makes them ideal for stretching out and relaxing.

verified_facts.text: The Nijo Suite offers panoramic views of Nijo Castle.
verified_facts.excerpt: The Nijo Suite offers panoramic views of Nijo Castle, spanning 112m2.

verified_facts.text: The Onsen Suite features an outdoor bath fed by natural hot springs.
verified_facts.excerpt: The Onsen Suite features an outdoor bath fed by natural hot springs

verified_facts.text: The Thermal Spring is sourced from a natural hot spring about 1,000 meters directly below the hotel.
verified_facts.excerpt: sourced from a natural hot spring about 1000 meters directly below the hotel property.

verified_facts.text: Guests wear swimsuits to bathe in the Thermal Spring.
verified_facts.excerpt: Guests wear swimsuits to bathe.

verified_facts.text: The private onsen offers complete privacy, with an enclosed wet living space and a dedicated Japanese garden.
verified_facts.excerpt: Our expansive private onsen, exceeding 100m2, offers complete privacy for a truly memorable experience. Featuring an enclosed wet living space and a dedicated Japanese garden

verified_facts.text: The central courtyard garden was designed by landscape architect Shunsaku Miyagi and measures 1,300 square meters.
verified_facts.excerpt: The central courtyard garden at our Kyoto luxury hotel, designed by landscape architect Shunsaku Miyagi, measures 1,300 square meters

verified_facts.text: The garden is a modern recreation of the garden of the former Mitsui residence.
verified_facts.excerpt: serving as a modern recreation of the garden that graced the former Mitsui residence

verified_facts.text: The courtyard garden is used for meditation and yoga.
verified_facts.excerpt: It is a place for meditation, yoga, and thoughtful reflection.

verified_facts.text: The courtyard garden centers on a huge cherry tree.
verified_facts.excerpt: central courtyard garden that pivots around a huge cherry tree

verified_facts.text: Spa treatments draw on the principles of Japanese Anma massage blended with facial treatments from abroad.
verified_facts.excerpt: Inspired by the ancient principles of Japanese Anma massage, we blend these techniques with innovative facial treatments from abroad

verified_facts.text: Restoration specialists Yasui Mokuzoku recreated the SHIKI-NO-MA to reflect the Okushoin room of the original Mitsui residence.
verified_facts.excerpt: Yasui Mokuzoku, renowned for its work on the repair and restoration of numerous historical buildings including the Kyoto Imperial Palace, has recreated the SHIKI-NO-MA to accurately reflect the Okushoin.

verified_facts.text: Ambassadors lead an art tour that begins at the Kajiimiya Gate and continues to the SHIKI-NO-MA.
verified_facts.excerpt: The tour begins at the iconic Kajiimiya Gate, the hotel's entranceway, and continues to the SHIKI-NO-MA

verified_facts.text: Ambassadors trained by a Mushakouji Senke tea master perform a seated tea procedure at CHAKYO.
verified_facts.excerpt: Our Ambassadors, who receive personal instruction from a Mushakouji Senke tea master, will perform a ryurei-style seated tea procedure at CHAKYO.

verified_facts.text: The hotel offers a private tour of Kiyomizu-dera Temple, guided by resident monks into sacred spaces normally closed to the public.
verified_facts.excerpt: Guided by resident monks, guests are welcomed into sacred spaces normally closed to the public

verified_facts.text: The signature restaurant TOKI serves innovative Kyoto French cuisine led by Chef Tetsuya Asano.
verified_facts.excerpt: our signature French restaurant in Kyoto, TOKI, is led by Chef Tetsuya Asano

verified_facts.text: The hotel's restaurants surround the garden so diners can view the seasons.
verified_facts.excerpt: all of which surround our beautifully curated garden so diners can enjoy viewing the rich tapestry of the seasons

verified_facts.text: Staff, many in seasonal kimonos, greet guests and perform tea ceremonies.
verified_facts.excerpt: many in exquisite seasonal kimonos, take care of guests

verified_facts.text: Nijo Castle is a five-minute walk from the hotel.
verified_facts.excerpt: Explore the World Heritage Site, just a five-minute walk from our hotel near Nijo-jo Castle

verified_facts.text: Kyoto Imperial Palace and the streets of Sanjo are within walking distance.
verified_facts.excerpt: Countless other attractions are within walking distance, from Kyoto Imperial Palace to the grid-lined streets of Sanjo.

verified_facts.text: The minimum age to check in is 18.
